title: Redwood technical deep dive: Dedicated vs Hosted (KV cache, batching, quant, VPC/on-prem)
summary: SE-led deep dive comparing Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated runtimes for Atlas Analytics. Focus on KV cache semantics, batching implications, quantization impact on latency/quality, and VPC/on-prem security. Customer concerned about noisy neighbor effects and throughput SLOs for peak trading hours. Agreed to run a 48-hour dedicated pilot benchmark and to share security docs, kernel/quant profiles, and a proposed test harness.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jorge Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Park (CTO - Atlas), Marcus Hill (Eng Manager), Nadia Singh (SRE)

Auto-generated summary: SE walked through Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, deep dive into KV cache and batching, quantization impact on RPS/latency, and VPC/on-prem considerations. Action items and pilot next steps agreed.

[00:00] Maya: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me?
[00:03] Lena: yes loud and clear, thanks maya. we have about an hour, we wanted to focus on performance and isolation, especially around the trading peak window.
[00:09] Marcus: and also the SRE concerns, noisy neighbor and throughput guarantees, so curious how dedicated helps vs hosted.
[00:15] Jorge: cool, i'll lead most of the technical deep dive, may jump in on the orchestration bits. quick agenda: runtime perf, kv cache semantics, batching, quantization tradeoffs, then vpc/on-prem and next steps. sound ok?
[00:28] Marcus: yep.
[00:29] Nadia: works for me.

[00:35] Jorge: ok starting runtime perf. short gist: hosted gives you fast time-to-market but it's multi-tenant so you see more variance at the p95/p99 due to neighbors and shared autoscaling. Dedicated maps your workloads to reserved GPU pools, so more predictable tail latencies and you can configure throughput reservations. that said, dedicated requires capacity planning and costs more up front.
[01:05] Lena: can you quantify "more predictable"? our SLAs are tight during market opens, p99 under 300ms for 1k qps spikes. is that realistic on hosted?
[01:15] Jorge: good question. on our hosted tier for comparable customers we've seen p99 around 350-600ms depending on model and seq length. with dedicated and pinned model variants we can get p99 down to ~200-300ms for the same loads, because of reserved batching and less noisy neighbors. caveat: these numbers assume KV cache hitrate and batching tuned.
[01:38] Marcus: when you say KV cache hitrate, what's realistic for short prefix workloads (we re-use prompts a lot)?
[01:45] Jorge: if your prefixes are stable we commonly see 60-85% KV cache hits; that reduces compute per request dramatically. but hitrate depends on model length, prompt variance, and cache TTL. hosted uses shared cache layers optimized per region; dedicated gives you exclusive KV caches which improves hit isolation for heavy reuse patterns.
[02:08] Nadia: how consistent are KV hit rates across shards? i'm worried some shards get hot and others cold, causing imbalanced latency.
[02:15] Jorge: yeah shard hotness is real. our runtime does adaptive shard sizing and LRU eviction; on Dedicated you can bump cache size or pin hot prefixes to reduce eviction churn. on Hosted, we try to smooth skew but you still see more variance. sorry tiny typo earlier - dedicatedy i meant dedicated.
[02:34] Lena: lol noted. so dedicated lets us increase per-customer kv capacity? that's useful.

[02:40] Jorge: exact. next: batching. continuous batching aggregates inflight requests to max throughput, but it increases single-request latency. we expose batch size and max wait knobs. with Dedicated, because throughput is guaranteed, we can use larger batch sizes and do more aggressive kernel fusion; that improves tokens/sec and cost-per-token while keeping average latency acceptable. Hosted tends to use more conservative batching to avoid noisy neighbor spikes.
[03:11] Marcus: can you give an example? model X, seq 512, what's tradeoff?
[03:16] Jorge: for a 70B-ish model at seq 512, a batch of 8 reduces per-token GPU time by ~2.2x vs batch 1; batch 16 gives ~3x. but batching adds queueing delay - at low QPS it's worse. recommended pattern: use dynamic batching with latency SLOs, and for Dedicated we can increase batch windows during known high-throughput windows.
[03:45] Lena: do you support dynamic policies like "during market open favor latency"?
[03:49] Jorge: yes, you can set routing policies and autoscaling policies - canary rules to change batching windows and model variants for different time windows.

[03:55] Jorge: quantization: lower precision (8-bit, 4-bit) reduces memory and increases throughput but can impact quality for some models. our quant profiles are validated per model; for many encoder-decoder and causal models, q4_0/q4_k_m gave close to original perplexity but some generation diversity suffers. for Atlas, if generation fidelity is critical we recommend mixed strategies: keep critical routes at fp16, use quantized variants for bulk embedding/rerank or less critical tails.
[04:29] Nadia: we've seen hallucination sensitivity when reducing precision; any advice?
[04:33] Jorge: yes test prompts that stress factuality. we run eval suites and will share quantization regression reports. quantization also interacts with KV cache because key/value vector precision changes hit semantics slightly. we have mitigations like re-encoding cache entries when toggling quant variants.

[04:55] Marcus: you mentioned kernel selection and optimized runtime earlier. can you expand on that?
[04:59] Jorge: sure - our runtime picks kernels based on sequence length distribution and hardware. for example, for short sequences we use fused attention kernels that reduce launch overhead. on Dedicated, we can tune kernels per customer and pin CUDA/cuDNN versions; Hosted runs a safe set for broad compatibility. that tuning can lift throughput and reduce p99.
[05:22] Lena: do you expose the kernel choices or is it opaque?
[05:25] Jorge: mostly opaque but we provide performance profiles, and for Dedicated we do a joint tuning session and share recommended kernel settings.

[05:32] Jorge: noisy neighbor scenarios: in Hosted multi-tenant env, heavy customers can increase GPU utilization leading to higher tail latency. our isolation controls include cgroup-based throttling and prioritization, but those are conservative. Dedicated eliminates that class by reserving whole GPU nodes; we also provide burst pools for temporary spikes.
[05:53] Marcus: is there any kernel-level preemption so a high-cost request doesn't block others?
[05:58] Jorge: preemption at GPU kernel level is limited; we rely on batching windows, request prioritization, and request slicing. on certain hardware we can use MIG partitions to isolate smaller workloads. Dedicated lets you choose MIG or full-GPU depending on your workload profile.
[06:15] Nadia: about throughput guarantees, what SLAs look like for Dedicated?
[06:19] Jorge: Dedicated offers throughput reservation and SLA on availability. for latency SLAs, we work with you to define targets based on model/config and reserve capacity. typical contractual p95/p99 commitments are available for enterprise contracts.
[06:33] Lena: ok, we need contractual guarantees for peak trading hours or we can't rely on hosted. so Dedicated is preferable if costs match.

[06:40] Jorge: noted. now VPC and on-prem: private deployment gives you a customer-managed control plane and network isolation; on-prem also gives running in your air-gapped env if needed. caveats: upgrades and debugging are slower, and we hand over certain infra responsibilities. for KMS/HSM integrations we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private.
[07:06] Marcus: for audit logs and SSO, do we get the same level as hosted?
[07:10] Jorge: yes, we expose audit logs, RBAC, and SAML/SCIM for Dedicated and Private. log retention and SIEM integration are configurable as add-ons.

[07:22] Lena: can you run benchmarks in our VPC or do you need a special harness?
[07:26] Jorge: we have a benchmark harness that can run from your VPC or from our test cluster. for true isolation tests we prefer running the workload on Dedicated hardware in your VPC. we'll share the harness repo and sample configs.

[07:39] Marcus: what's the onboarding time for Dedicated? months? weeks?
[07:42] Maya: onboarding typically 2-6 weeks depending on provisioning and security review. pilot bench—48-72 hours of dedicated runs—can be set up quicker once network peering and keys are done.

[07:55] Jorge: quick pause for clarifying Qs. Marcus?
[07:58] Marcus: just real quick, how do you handle model rollouts so we don't regress?
[08:02] Jorge: we support canary rollouts, A/B, automatic fallback and eval-based regression alerts. if a quantized variant regresses, you can automatically fallback to fp16. integrated evals can gate rollouts.

[08:13] Nadia: curious, for our retriever+generation pipeline, where would caching be most effective?
[08:18] Jorge: typically prefix and KV cache between retriever and generator shows big wins; also caching embedding vectors for rerank reduces calls. for retrieval-heavy workloads we recommend a hybrid: cache top-k results at edge and use smaller model variants for rerank.

[08:33] Lena: any pitfalls you've seen with customers migrating from hosted to dedicated?
[08:36] Jorge: a few: underestimating spike loads, not tuning batch windows for their traffic shape, and forgetting to re-run evals for quant variants. also network peers and IAM misconfig cause delays. we provide a migration checklist.

[08:51] Marcus: can you show sample numbers for cost delta? hosted vs dedicated for our expected 100M tokens/month?
[08:58] Maya: we'll share a tailored pricing sheet; ballpark: dedicated reduces per-token costs when you hit sustained usage because of reserved capacity and higher batching. hosted is cheaper for bursty/low volume and avoids infra ops. we'll include detailed TCO in the pilot proposal.

[09:15] Jorge: i'm going to call out two technical caveats: 1) quantization can change KV cache semantics — need re-encoding strategy; 2) kernel tuning yields biggest wins for short sequences, so if your traffic is mostly short prefixes, tuning matters a lot.

[09:34] Lena: makes sense. Marcus and Nadia can you consolidate our top 3 SLOs and share?
[09:39] Marcus: yes we'll do that after.

[09:42] Jorge: ok wrapping up with proposed pilot: 48-hour Dedicated run in a staging VPC with your anonymized traffic, compare p50/p95/p99 and throughput vs hosted baseline, run quantized and fp16 variants, and return detailed perf profiles. we can also run rogue load to simulate noisy neighbor to validate isolation.
[10:06] Nadia: that noise test is important. we want to see worst-case tail.
[10:09] Jorge: agreed. we'll script that.

[10:12] Maya: recap of next steps - Maya send pilot proposal and pricing; Jorge upload harness; Atlas share 24h traces and SLOs; schedule kickoff. any other items?
[10:25] Lena: please also include sample security docs and SOC/ISO attestations.
[10:29] Maya: yes will include SOC2 + ISO docs and KMS integration notes.

[10:33] Marcus: one last quick question — how do you handle perf regressions post-deploy?
[10:38] Jorge: we have perf regression alerts tied to evaluation sets, tracing to identify hot kernels, and rollback automation. for Dedicated we also offer quarterly tuning sessions.

[10:50] Maya: perfect, we'll follow up in Slack with links and schedule. thanks everyone.
[10:55] Lena: thanks all.
[10:56] Meeting end.
